'''Sayur asem''' or '''sayur asam''' is an [[Indonesian cuisine|Indonesian]] [[vegetable soup]]. It is a popular [[Southeast asia|Southeast Asian]] dish originating from [[Sundanese cuisine]], consisting of vegetables in [[tamarind]] [[soup]].<ref>{{cite web | title=40 of Indonesia's best dishes | website=CNN Travel | date=August 9, 2011 | url=http://travel.cnn.com/explorations/eat/40-foods-indonesians-cant-live-without-327106 | access-date=January 30, 2015}}</ref> 

The sweet and sour flavour of this dish is considered refreshing and very compatible with fried or grilled dishes, including [[salted fish]], ''[[ikan goreng]]'', ''[[ayam goreng]]'' and ''[[lalab|lalapan]]'', a kind of vegetable salad usually served raw but can also be cooked, and is usually eaten with [[steamed rice]] and ''[[sambal|sambal terasi]]'' chilli paste. 

The origin of the dish can be traced to the [[Sundanese people]] of [[West Java]], [[Banten]], and the [[Jakarta]] region. It is well known to be a part of the [[Sundanese cuisine]] and the daily diet of the [[Betawi people|Betawi]].

Earlier versions of the dish did not include corn, as it was not introduced to the Indonesian archipelago until the 16th Century.
